title: Mayor wants to see Stockport regeneration inspire other areas

evidence_packet.title: Mayor wants to see Stockport regeneration inspire other areas
evidence_packet.lead: Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig wants other areas to follow Stockport's lead
evidence_packet.summary: Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig wants other areas to follow Stockport's lead
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The mayor of Greater Manchester has said she hopes the £1bn regeneration of Stockport town centre can be replicated in towns across the region The Stockport Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) was launched seven years ago and has ambitions to build 8,000 new homes in the town centre by 2040 Bev Craig, who became metro mayor of Greater Manchester in July, said: "I want to carry on and go further with the work of Mayoral Development Corporations across the region "I want to build genuinely affordable homes on publicly owned land and, by getting the private sector to back us, I'm excited about what we can achieve with our MDCs, in places like Ashton-under-Lyne, Stalybridge and Oldham." Mayoral Development Corporations are used to speed up regeneration projects by bringing land, funding, and planning powers together to attract investment They are able to use compulsory purchase powers to make sites available for housing projects and many MDCs are able to grant planning permission for developments

title: Moorland hit by fresh wildfire as heatwave peaks

evidence_packet.title: Moorland hit by fresh wildfire as heatwave peaks
evidence_packet.lead: It comes just weeks after major wildfires burned across nearby land at Done Stone Reservoir for weeks
evidence_packet.summary: It comes just weeks after major wildfires burned across nearby land at Done Stone Reservoir for weeks
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Firefighters have brought a fresh wildfire in Greater Manchester under control in an area plagued by the blazes all summer Fire crews were sent to the blaze near Holmfirth Road in Oldham, at about 22:25 BST on Wednesday - with the fire covering an area of about 1,640 by 492ft (500m by 150m) at its height Engines remained at the scene on Thursday afternoon dampening down hotspots and working to prevent the fire from spreading It comes just weeks after major wildfires burned across nearby land at Dove Stone Reservoir and Swineshaw for almost three weeks, with a major incident declared The major incident was stood down earlier this month are the fires were largely contained Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said the latest fire was not connected to those earlier blazes and the cause was being investigated

title: Manchester mayor calls for warehouse planning changes

evidence_packet.title: Manchester mayor calls for warehouse planning changes
evidence_packet.lead: Bev Craig says planning rules should be reviewed after complaints about warehouses built near housing
evidence_packet.summary: Bev Craig says planning rules should be reviewed after complaints about warehouses built near housing
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester mayor calls for warehouse planning changes - BBC News Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Residents on the Henfold Estate have raised concerns about warehouses being built at the nearby Astley Business Park By James Fell North West Published 13 August 2026 The mayor of Greater Manchester has said planning rules should be reviewed after complaints about warehouses being built close to people's homes. Speaking on BBC Radio Manchester's Hot Seat, Bev Craig said she agreed with concerns raised by campaigners from the Astley Warehouse Action Group and questioned why modern industrial developments were being allowed closer to residential properties than traditional industry. The group was formed after the construction of large warehouses at Astley Business Park near Tyldesley. Residents have complained about the scale of the development, its proximity to homes and concerns over noise from future operations. During Thursday's programme, campaigner John asked whether residents could continue to rely on mayoral support as they were entering what he described as a new phase of the campaign, focused on the effect the warehouses would have once fully operational. Craig said that lessons needed to be learned from the situation. "I think we have to go and look at proper planning rules around this as well, because old industry wouldn't have got that close to your house," she said. "So why is it that new industry can?" The mayor said she wanted to explore whether planning rules should be changed, and offered to meet residents to discuss their concerns. She added: "Other people can't be in the same situation in the future, and we need to look at what we can do to help you now." title: Worker fears 'no work-life balance' under BT relocation plan

evidence_packet.title: Worker fears 'no work-life balance' under BT relocation plan
evidence_packet.lead: Lesley Wood says her commute to a new Manchester office would mean travelling for hours a day, as dozens hold a protest
evidence_packet.summary: Lesley Wood says her commute to a new Manchester office would mean travelling for hours a day, as dozens hold a protest
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Worker fears 'no work-life balance' under BT relocation plan - BBC News Image caption, Lesley Wood has worked for BT for 39 years and feels she has "no choice" but to relocate to Manchester By Thomas Berrington Reporting from Liverpool Published 13 August 2026 A British Telecom (BT) worker has described the planned closure of the Liverpool office and relocation of about 600 jobs as "absolutely horrendous", as dozens of workers held a protest. BT is due to close its Old Hall Street office in March when its lease runs out. The firm has said part of the reason is due to a hike in lease renewal costs. Roles will be moved to Manchester and Leeds and staff are being offered a chance to relocate but unions say it is not an option for many. Lesley Wood is being moved to the Manchester office and said she would have "no work-life balance" travelling three to four hours a day to and from her home in Southport. BT said it was taking concerns raised seriously. The telecom firm said the changes were part of an "optimisation and modernisation" of its working spaces. Wood has worked for BT for 39 years and been based at the Liverpool office since 2017. She told BBC Radio Merseyside the closure would have a big impact on her life. "It means I have to get up at 5.30am every morning. I'll have to get a train that takes one hour, 15 minutes. "I'm too close to retirement to get another job, so I've got no choice but to go there. "I'm just literally going to be coming home and going to bed." She said it was not the first time she had been relocated. "They did it to us in Warrington when they closed down BT Business." However, the prospect of closing the whole site was "absolutely horrendous" and would be a "really sad day" for all the staff there, she said. Image caption, Heather Taylor say

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig has appealed to public sector bodies to "offer up" derelict land so tens of thousands of council houses can be built The new mayor is aiming to build 10,000 "genuinely affordable" homes in the city region by May 2028, part of a longer-term plan to create 50,000 council and social houses A "public sector land bank" is being created to find brownfield sites that will be given priority for building The Home Builders Federation said the plan was welcome but that "similar ambitions had floundered" in the past The mayor said she wanted Greater Manchester to "lead the way in building a new generation" of council and social homes "If you're sitting on a small piece of land that's surplus to requirement, then offer it into the pot and let's get building," Craig said

At its height, the fire covered an area measuring 500m by 150m, the fire service said, with eight crews at the scene Drone pictures show the huge area of moorland scorched in the blaze, with smoke blowing across the road. Tonight (Thursday) crews remain at the scene after almost 24 hours, but the blaze has been brought under control. Holmfirth Road remains closed, however In a statement Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said: "Crews remain at the scene of a moorland fire near Holmfirth Road in Oldham , having worked through the night and in extremely hot conditions today to bring the wildfire under control " Firefighters are currently damping down hotspots and using tactical measures to prevent the wildfire spreading. evidence_packet.title: Fire service issues new statement as latest Saddleworth Moor blaze now 'under control'
evidence_packet.lead: Saddleworth and Lees Fire service issues new statement as latest Saddleworth Moor blaze now 'under control' The blaze broke out on Wednesday night News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 20:27, 13 Aug 2026 View Image Smoke billowing across Holmfirth Road on Sad A wildfire at Saddleworth Mo
evidence_packet.summary: Saddleworth and Lees Fire service issues new statement as latest Saddleworth Moor blaze now 'under control' The blaze broke out on Wednesday night News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 20:27, 13 Aug 2026 View Image Smoke billowing across Holmfirth Road on Sad A wildfire at Saddleworth Mo
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Saddleworth and Lees Fire service issues new statement as latest Saddleworth Moor blaze now 'under control' The blaze broke out on Wednesday night News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 20:27, 13 Aug 2026 View Image Smoke billowing across Holmfirth Road on Sad A wildfire at Saddleworth Moor is now 'under control', the fire service has said Firefighters spent last night and today battling the blaze off Holmfirth Road in heatwave conditions. At its height, the fire covered an area measuring 500m by 150m, the fire service said, with eight crews at the scene Drone pictures show the huge area of moorland scorched in the blaze, with smoke blowing across the road. Tonight (Thursday) crews remain at the scene after almost 24 hours, but the blaze has been brought under control. Holmfirth Road remains closed, however In a statement Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said: "Crews remain at the scene of a moorland fire near Holmfirth Road in Oldham , having worked through the night and in extremely hot conditions today to bring the wildfire under control " Firefighters are currently damping down hotspots and using tactical measures to prevent the wildfire spreading. Residents nearby should avoid the area and shut their windows and doors if smoke is visible

evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Decision due on increased ’24-hour operation’ of waste plant in village on outskirts of Bolton J Dickinson and Sons said increased hours would aid expansion with changes ‘required to accommodate an increased demand for recovery and recycling' C Plans for a waste and recycl
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Decision due on increased ’24-hour operation’ of waste plant in village on outskirts of Bolton J Dickinson and Sons said increased hours would aid expansion with changes ‘required to accommodate an increased demand for recovery and recycling' C Plans for a waste and recycl
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Decision due on increased ’24-hour operation’ of waste plant in village on outskirts of Bolton J Dickinson and Sons said increased hours would aid expansion with changes ‘required to accommodate an increased demand for recovery and recycling' C Plans for a waste and recycling plant to increase 24-hour operating hours to include Sundays and Bank Holidays are set to be considered J Dickinson and Sons Ltd are a long standing occupier of Rivington View Business Park, by the M61 on Station Road, Blackrod The firm employs more than 100 staff at the site which serves commercial, industrial and local authority customers, as well as householders via a skip hire service Operations have been continuous at the site since 1999 and are regulated by an Environment Agency permit In 2024 planning permission was granted to allow for 24-hour operations within the waste transfer station of the site on Monday to Friday and midnight to 7pm on Saturdays, with maintenance and cleaning carried out on Sundays and Bank Holidays

Two probes were launched on the same day following the separate deaths of two women Police are investigating four incidents - in neighbourhoods in Bolton, Tameside, Rochdale and Salford. Two women, 39 and 61, and two men, one in his 30s and one 31-years-old, died in the incidents There is no suggestion any of the cases are linked. Crime scene investigators and forensic specialists have been seen working at crime scenes across the region in recent days Coroners across Greater Manchester have been handed files in relation to the cases Emma McGowan, 39, was found unresponsive at a property in Breightmet in Bolton in the early hours of August 4

title: Their biggest worry was once escaped cows, now it's huge developments on their doorstep

evidence_packet.title: Their biggest worry was once escaped cows, now it's huge developments on their doorstep
evidence_packet.lead: Trafford Their biggest worry was once escaped cows, now it's huge developments on their doorstep 12,000sqm of warehouses are proposed on a field in the area View 2 Images Land off Dairyhouse Lane which is included in the draft local plan for warehousi News Hannah Richardson 17:39
evidence_packet.summary: Trafford Their biggest worry was once escaped cows, now it's huge developments on their doorstep 12,000sqm of warehouses are proposed on a field in the area View 2 Images Land off Dairyhouse Lane which is included in the draft local plan for warehousi News Hannah Richardson 17:39
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trafford Their biggest worry was once escaped cows, now it's huge developments on their doorstep 12,000sqm of warehouses are proposed on a field in the area View 2 Images Land off Dairyhouse Lane which is included in the draft local plan for warehousi News Hannah Richardson 17:39, 13 Aug 2026 Their biggest worry was once escaped cows but now their fields are being lost to ever-expanding industrial development Residents living in Dairyhouse Lane, in Broadheath, said that when they first moved to the area, they were surrounded by farmland. Cattle would get out into the road and they would have to put them back, a woman who has lived there almost 60 years said But warehouses have sprung up around their peaceful community and more could be built in the coming years A large greenspace off the winding country road has been included in the draft Trafford local plan as a potential development site. Trafford council believes it could be suitable for 12,000sqm of industrial and warehousing floorspace The town hall has said the land is next to an existing industrial estate, is connected to the A56 by George Richards Way and is not part of the green belt. The authority hopes the allocation will ‘attract high-quality employment investment’ to the area

(Image: Andy Commins) Comments News Owen Hughes Business correspondent and Ryan Price 17:06, 13 Aug 2026 A woman was taken to hospital after suffering a jellyfish sting to the eye while situated off the coast of North Wales The woman was aboard a yacht anchored off Moelfre Bay, on the northeast coast of the Isle of Anglesey, on Tuesday afternoon (11 August). She had been retrieving a line from the water which was covered in jellyfish tentacles, one of which made contact with her eye The incident caused intense pain, prompting Moelfre RNLI to respond shortly before 3pm - with the yacht situated just a short distance from the lifeboat station The woman was brought ashore and transferred to the lifeboat station, where a swift medical assessment took place It was subsequently decided that she would make her own way by taxi to the emergency department at Ysbyty Gwynedd in Bangor for further treatment, reports North Wales Live

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A Level results Greater Manchester students pull through incredible odds to achieve amazing A Level results Pupils will received their final grades today News Bethan Finighan , Ramazani Mwamba News reporter , Emily Parker Shopping Writer , Ludwik Lipi There were emotional scenes across schools in Greater Manchester as students who battled through hospital visits and house fires received their A Level results This year's cohort is among the tens of thousands of students who found out how they did in their A Level and vocational technical qualifications (VTQs) on Thursday morning (August 13) The Manchester Evening News travelled to several colleges and sixth forms to speak to locals on this momentous day. At Aquinas College, Stockport , perhaps nobody was happier than young carer, Zanwer Afa This year, he spent a month revising in temporary housing due to a house fire. Today, he was in great spirits as he spoke to the M.E.N after achieving four A*s and securing a scholarship at Imperial College in London "First reaction was 'they weren't mine,'" he told the M.E.N

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale Man, 31, found dead in Rochdale murder probe named as heartbroken mum pays tribute Nathan Haigh was found unresponsive at a Rochdale flat earlier this week. A woman has been arrested for murder News Damon Wilkinson Reporter and Todd Fitzgeral A man whose death has sparked a murder investigation in Rochdale has been named by his heartbroken mother. Nathan Haigh was found unresponsive by emergency services at a flat on Great Howarth, near Wardle, just before 7.40pm on Tuesday (August 11) The 31-year-old was pronounced dead shortly after, despite the best efforts of paramedics. Greater Manchester Police said a 37-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of murder. She was being quizzed by detectives on Thursday (August 13) A force spokesperson said detectives are 'exploring several lines of enquiries in what initially appears to be suspicious circumstances' There is not believed to be any risk to the public. On Thursday afternoon the investigation continued, with a police officer stood guard at the entrance to the block of flats on the estate near the village of Wardle, on the outskirts of Rochdale Neighbours said earlier in the day forensics officers were seen examining the ground floor flat where Mr Haigh is thought to have lived

In the coming weeks many more will fly from the northern travel hub before the break ends in September So far this summer Antalya in Turkey and Palma in Mallorca have proved to be the most popular destinations, with Palma set to be the top destination overall this summer. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Saddleworth and Lees Fire service issues new statement as latest Saddleworth Moor blaze now 'under control' The blaze broke out on Wednesday night News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 20:27, 13 Aug 2026 View Image Smoke billowing across Holmfirth Road on Sad A wildfire at Saddleworth Moor is now 'under control', the fire service has said Firefighters spent last night and today battling the blaze off Holmfirth Road in heatwave conditions. At its height, the fire covered an area measuring 500m by 150m, the fire service said, with eight crews at the scene Drone pictures show the huge area of moorland scorched in the blaze, with smoke blowing across the road. Tonight (Thursday) crews remain at the scene after almost 24 hours, but the blaze has been brought under control. Holmfirth Road remains closed, however In a statement Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said: "Crews remain at the scene of a moorland fire near Holmfirth Road in Oldham , having worked through the night and in extremely hot conditions today to bring the wildfire under control " Firefighters are currently damping down hotspots and using tactical measures to prevent the wildfire spreading. Residents nearby should avoid the area and shut their windows and doors if smoke is visible

evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Decision due on increased ’24-hour operation’ of waste plant in village on outskirts of Bolton J Dickinson and Sons said increased hours would aid expansion with changes ‘required to accommodate an increased demand for recovery and recycling' C Plans for a waste and recycl
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Decision due on increased ’24-hour operation’ of waste plant in village on outskirts of Bolton J Dickinson and Sons said increased hours would aid expansion with changes ‘required to accommodate an increased demand for recovery and recycling' C Plans for a waste and recycling plant to increase 24-hour operating hours to include Sundays and Bank Holidays are set to be considered J Dickinson and Sons Ltd are a long standing occupier of Rivington View Business Park, by the M61 on Station Road, Blackrod The firm employs more than 100 staff at the site which serves commercial, industrial and local authority customers, as well as householders via a skip hire service Operations have been continuous at the site since 1999 and are regulated by an Environment Agency permit In 2024 planning permission was granted to allow for 24-hour operations within the waste transfer station of the site on Monday to Friday and midnight to 7pm on Saturdays, with maintenance and cleaning carried out on Sundays and Bank Holidays

Two probes were launched on the same day following the separate deaths of two women Police are investigating four incidents - in neighbourhoods in Bolton, Tameside, Rochdale and Salford. Two women, 39 and 61, and two men, one in his 30s and one 31-years-old, died in the incidents There is no suggestion any of the cases are linked. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police The 'catastrophic lack of judgement' that led to a GMP cop being sacked in shame Pc Jack Sanderson has been sacked after been found guilty of gross misconduct News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 17:54, 13 Aug 2026 View Image Pc Jac A GMP officer has been sacked in disgrace after failing a drugs test Pc Jack Sanderson was said to have demonstrated a 'catastrophic lack of judgement' after a urine test in March revealed he had taken cannabis and cocaine. Following a disciplinary tribunal overseen by Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson , Pc Sanderson was found guilty of gross mis Sir Stephen said he had been presented 'incontrovertible evidence' of drug use and that Pc Sanderson's culpability 'must be regarded as high' He added: "His actions were deliberate and carried out in the full knowledge that his conduct was contrary to that explicitly set forth in the GMP drug alcohol misuse policy." Taking drugs was 'extremely unwise', Sir Stephen said, as it 'must necessarily have involved a causal and corrupting association with a person or persons actively engaged in criminality'

title: Their biggest worry was once escaped cows, now it's huge developments on their doorstep

evidence_packet.title: Their biggest worry was once escaped cows, now it's huge developments on their doorstep
evidence_packet.lead: Trafford Their biggest worry was once escaped cows, now it's huge developments on their doorstep 12,000sqm of warehouses are proposed on a field in the area View 2 Images Land off Dairyhouse Lane which is included in the draft local plan for warehousi News Hannah Richardson 17:39
evidence_packet.summary: Trafford Their biggest worry was once escaped cows, now it's huge developments on their doorstep 12,000sqm of warehouses are proposed on a field in the area View 2 Images Land off Dairyhouse Lane which is included in the draft local plan for warehousi News Hannah Richardson 17:39
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trafford Their biggest worry was once escaped cows, now it's huge developments on their doorstep 12,000sqm of warehouses are proposed on a field in the area View 2 Images Land off Dairyhouse Lane which is included in the draft local plan for warehousi News Hannah Richardson 17:39, 13 Aug 2026 Their biggest worry was once escaped cows but now their fields are being lost to ever-expanding industrial development Residents living in Dairyhouse Lane, in Broadheath, said that when they first moved to the area, they were surrounded by farmland. Cattle would get out into the road and they would have to put them back, a woman who has lived there almost 60 years said But warehouses have sprung up around their peaceful community and more could be built in the coming years A large greenspace off the winding country road has been included in the draft Trafford local plan as a potential development site. Trafford council believes it could be suitable for 12,000sqm of industrial and warehousing floorspace The town hall has said the land is next to an existing industrial estate, is connected to the A56 by George Richards Way and is not part of the green belt. The authority hopes the allocation will ‘attract high-quality employment investment’ to the area

evidence_packet.lead: North Wales Woman hospitalised after being stung in the eye by jellyfish off North Wales coast The woman was recovering a line in the water when she came into contact with the sea creature View 2 Images A lions mane jellyfish.
evidence_packet.summary: North Wales Woman hospitalised after being stung in the eye by jellyfish off North Wales coast The woman was recovering a line in the water when she came into contact with the sea creature View 2 Images A lions mane jellyfish. evidence_packet.evidence_text: North Wales Woman hospitalised after being stung in the eye by jellyfish off North Wales coast The woman was recovering a line in the water when she came into contact with the sea creature View 2 Images A lions mane jellyfish. (Image: Andy Commins) Comments News Owen Hughes Business correspondent and Ryan Price 17:06, 13 Aug 2026 A woman was taken to hospital after suffering a jellyfish sting to the eye while situated off the coast of North Wales The woman was aboard a yacht anchored off Moelfre Bay, on the northeast coast of the Isle of Anglesey, on Tuesday afternoon (11 August). She had been retrieving a line from the water which was covered in jellyfish tentacles, one of which made contact with her eye The incident caused intense pain, prompting Moelfre RNLI to respond shortly before 3pm - with the yacht situated just a short distance from the lifeboat station The woman was brought ashore and transferred to the lifeboat station, where a swift medical assessment took place It was subsequently decided that she would make her own way by taxi to the emergency department at Ysbyty Gwynedd in Bangor for further treatment, reports North Wales Live

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale Man, 31, found dead in Rochdale murder probe named as heartbroken mum pays tribute Nathan Haigh was found unresponsive at a Rochdale flat earlier this week. A woman has been arrested for murder News Damon Wilkinson Reporter and Todd Fitzgeral A man whose death has sparked a murder investigation in Rochdale has been named by his heartbroken mother. Nathan Haigh was found unresponsive by emergency services at a flat on Great Howarth, near Wardle, just before 7.40pm on Tuesday (August 11) The 31-year-old was pronounced dead shortly after, despite the best efforts of paramedics. Greater Manchester Police said a 37-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of murder. She was being quizzed by detectives on Thursday (August 13) A force spokesperson said detectives are 'exploring several lines of enquiries in what initially appears to be suspicious circumstances' There is not believed to be any risk to the public. On Thursday afternoon the investigation continued, with a police officer stood guard at the entrance to the block of flats on the estate near the village of Wardle, on the outskirts of Rochdale Neighbours said earlier in the day forensics officers were seen examining the ground floor flat where Mr Haigh is thought to have lived

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

evidence_packet.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council's children's services have been rated inadequate in two key areas by Ofsted, with inspectors warning that delays in responding to concerns about children have left some at risk of harm The report, published yesterday following a two-week inspection between June 8th and 19th, judged both the impact of leaders on social work practice and the experiences of children who need help and protection to be inadequate - the watchdog's lowest grade Services for children in care were rated good, while support for care leavers requires improvement to be good Inspectors, led by His Majesty's Inspector Leanne Cooper, found that since the council's last full inspection in 2022 - when it was rated requires improvement across the board - leaders had failed to recognise and act on shortfalls in critical parts of the service The sharpest criticism was reserved for the council's "front door" - the point at which concerns about children are first reported. The report found that responses to contacts about children take too long, are not prioritised in line with risk, and that many children face lengthy Strategy discussions - urgent multi-agency meetings held when a child is identified as being at risk of significant harm - are too often delayed, leaving children in potentially unsafe situations for too long and at risk of what inspectors called unassessed significant harm

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Sealing the deal: Summer resurfacing sees 21kms of new road surface laid down across Manchester | Manchester City Council Sealing the deal: Summer resurfacing sees 21kms of new road surface laid down across Manchester Thursday 13 August 2026 A huge programme of works is under way across Manchester to make sure our road network is in good condition as we head towards colder and wetter months. From the start of August through to the end of the month, highways crews will be out in force, carrying out surface dressing at nearly 30 locations across the city. Surface dressing is a cost-effective treatment that helps protect roads from everyday wear and tear. By sealing the road surface, it prevents water from entering small cracks and causing further deterioration. With the majority damage cause to the road surface during the winter months, work like this is vital to ensure the health of our road network, extending the life of our roads and reduce the need for more disruptive repairs in the future. Over the course of just two weeks, highways crews will treat approximately 154,000 square metres of road surface, covering more than 21 kilometres of carriageway across Manchester, roughly the distance from Manchester city centre to Glossop. The programme also incorporates the use of recycled granite chippings as part of Manchester City Council's commitment to more sustainable highway maintenance. Some of the roads included in this year's programme are: Alan Turing Way Wythenshawe Road Princess Road Yew Tree Road Barlow Moor Road For a full list of roads included in the programme visit out website here. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham has recorded participation rates above both regional and national averages while significantly reducing the number of young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET) The latest Department for Education (DfE) Local Authority Participation and NEET figures for the 2025/26 academic year show that 93.2 per cent of Oldham's 16 and 17-year-olds are participating in education and training, an increase of 2.8 percentage points on the previous year. T At the same time, Oldham's combined NEET and Not Known (NK) rate has fallen to 4.6%, down 1.1 percentage points from 2024/25. This is significantly lower than both the North West average of 5.5% and the England average of 5.8% The figures also highlight Oldham's strong performance, in partnership with the charity Positive Steps, in tracking and supporting young people Positive Steps provides young people with support, careers advice and guidance after school, or between 19 and 25 if they have an Education Healthcare Plan (EHCP), helping them to move into education, training or employment Only 59 young people out of 7,177 are currently unaccounted for – 0.8 per cent of the borough's young people. This is well below the North West average of 1.3 per cent and the England average of 2.4 per cent

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urging residents to ensure unwanted electricals are taken to the correct recycling facilities Research from Material Focus has highlighted the growing popularity of low-cost electrical products, often known as ‘FastTech’, which can be easily forgotten, thrown away, or incorrectly disposed of. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Cost: £150 for the full course. Bursaries are available for those on lower income – please email learning@bandonthewall.org to arrange this.. . Spaces are limited – Book here . . . Having started comedy in 2016 Mike has amassed a large online following from podcast and stand-up clips, regularly getting millions of views on various platforms Mike began stand-up comedy in Chicago, where within two years he was working regularly at the most prestigious clubs in the city, including The Laugh Factory. evidence_packet.title: New Latin BBQ and bar Dahlia to bring open-fire cooking and late-night DJs to the Northern Quarter
evidence_packet.lead: The original team behind Ramona and The Firehouse will open the two-floor restaurant, bar and music venue this September Go to Manchester's Finest X profile A new Latin American-inspired barbecue restaurant, bar and late-night venue is set to open in Manchester’s Northern Quarter
evidence_packet.summary: The original team behind Ramona and The Firehouse will open the two-floor restaurant, bar and music venue this September Go to Manchester's Finest X profile A new Latin American-inspired barbecue restaurant, bar and late-night venue is set to open in Manchester’s Northern Quarter
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The original team behind Ramona and The Firehouse will open the two-floor restaurant, bar and music venue this September Go to Manchester's Finest X profile A new Latin American-inspired barbecue restaurant, bar and late-night venue is set to open in Manchester’s Northern Quarter this September Dahlia is the latest project from WANT Studios, the creative hospitality studio run by Andy Marshall, Andy Windsor, Liam McCue and Adelaide Winter The WANT Studios team were the original creatives behind Manchester venues including Ramona and The Firehouse. evidence_packet.evidence_text: $7m funding round as Manchester startup addresses cyber risk of growing AI role in software development - Prolific North Skip to content Audio Veteran broadcaster John MacKay returns News MoneySuperMarket launches business bank with fintech partners News Former Sage software boss joins Newcastle clean tech scale-up $7m funding round as Manchester startup addresses cyber risk of growing AI role in software development Tech by Chris Newbould August 12, 2026 Manchester cybersecurity start-up Cytix has announced a $7M (£5m) Series A funding round to accelerate the company’s mission to tackle the problems created by rapid software change – a reality that is becoming a distinct risk for organisations as AI-assisted development, agentic workflows, and continuous delivery lead to an increased volume of AI-generated code. The round has been led by Northern Gritstone , the venture capital and investment firm that focuses on science and tech startups in the North of England, with participation from existing investors, Auriga Cyber Ventures and NPIF II – PXN Equity Finance, which is managed by PXN Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II (NPIF II). Ben Armstrong, CEO of Cytix said: “We chose Northern Gritstone for their conviction in investing in deeptech companies in the North of England with global ambition. Northern Gritstone and Cytix share the belief that software change is becoming a key risk for organisations, and those that build software need a solution that scales with the current pace of development. We’re also grateful to the existing investors that have backed us since the early days and increased their commitment because they’ve seen the thesis play out.” READ MORE: Not just a diversity issue – an economic one: New South Yorkshire taskforce to ad

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fancy a space to connect with the community away from Canal Street? Kiki Family Social is a relaxed, grassroots meet-up with no rigid expectations, pressure, or hierarchy. The space is shaped by the people who come along — everyone helps make it what it is We meet every Thursday, and there’s always space at the table whether you’re new to Manchester or just dipping your toe into social meet-ups You’ll usually find a mix of familiar faces and new ones each week. We typically gather at a reserved table inside with pride flags, and there’s often a table outside too. On busy nights we’ll make sure flags are on the outside table as well. If you’re unsure where we are, just a 📅 Every Thursday, 7:30pm (You’re welcome to arrive earlier or later) 🍻 This isn’t a sober event, but there’s no pressure to drink. The bar offers zero-alcohol options as well as tea and coffee
